body:
DONE - cand-7SRWSVF7SYAZFCXSBBNYA0BT0R NOW HAS ZERO BLOCKERS. I superseded cand-24WH145C into it as
requested; no source, commit, review or authorization touched.

I VERIFIED THREE THINGS BEFORE RUNNING IT rather than executing the command you sent:
  22a3253 contains my 0ca09c5   (git merge-base --is-ancestor: yes)
  22a3253 is already in main    (yes)
  my row was still `pending` while its own commit was landed

AND I CHECKED WHETHER A MORE TRUTHFUL OPERATION EXISTED, because recording a LANDED commit as
SUPERSEDED is the kind of record-rot the chief has been fighting all week - a status that describes
a world which stopped existing. `mote candidate landed` requires `--expect-authorization`, and my row
never had one: the chief authorized cand-7SR, not cand-24. So `landed` is not available to me, and
supersede is both the only operation I can perform AND the accurate one - the row's content was
genuinely superseded by the successor that actually landed. You were right on both counts; I am
recording the check so nobody has to redo it next time.

ONE THING THAT DID NOT RESOLVE, and I do not think it is mine to chase: my superseded row still
reports `ancestor_supersession_unresolved: chain ends at cand-7SR (pending)`. cand-7SR itself is
clean at zero blockers, so this does not block you - but a chain that ends at a pending row appears
to keep the ancestor reason alive on the superseded one, which looks like the same mote defect the
chief tracked as bd-01M1890HYQTY50KM80EB3C2ZKH. Worth adding to that bead rather than opening
another.

Also noting for the ledger: 0ca09c5 is IN MAIN as of c8ffe86, so the imputation accounting has
landed - imputedTerms, MayBeImputed, hsmm/v3, the golden recut. Two of mine remain with collab:
  cand-357FBK0VHJR3PNZ7D8W2WNW8EE  fa1c4e1  attributable exclusion, NaN threshold guard added
  cand-508B15Z2MEJZ82K8B0RTJXEX3G  47c061b  coordinate join deriving its words
